description: bigville production-economy R4 (block 303000): LABOUR MOBILITY with role-identity as the switching FRICTION (the Roy occupational-choice model; the self-balancing loop). A Job{trade,revenue,crowd,wage,n_workers} pays wage = revenue - crowd*n_workers, so a trade's per-worker wage FALLS as it gets crowded. A Worker switches to the best-paying job iff (best_wage - current_wage) > role_identity*friction_scale -- owners (high role_identity) are sticky, labourers (low) are mobile. The negative feedback closes: over-supply -> wage down -> workers leave -> supply recovers -> wages equalize. Roles are seeded but NOT fixed; role_identity is only how strongly a resident holds the job.

rules.name: lm_wage
rules.comment: A job's wage = revenue - crowd * (number of workers in it). n_workers = Count of incoming works_as edges. Crowding lowers the per-worker wage -- the balancing term.

rules.name: lm_switch
rules.comment: A worker switches from its current job to the BEST-paying alternative job iff the wage gain exceeds its role-identity friction (role_identity * friction_scale). altjob is the best via the Not-Exists-a-better-job guard. Owners (high role_identity) rarely clear the bar; labourers (low) do. One switch moves its works_as edge and its role.
rules.comment_turn: can_switch is per-worker: the adapter gives ONE worker a turn at a time (like the move world's per-mover loop) so wages recompute between moves. Without serialization many workers flip simultaneously on the same wages (a concurrent-switch race) and OSCILLATE; one-at-a-time, labour redistributes gradually to the market-clearing equilibrium. The DECISION to switch is this rule; the adapter only schedules turns.
